answer: Sybil resistance starts by making identity expensive: each agent posts a refundable stake that is slashed on proven fraud, so spawning fakes costs real money. Reputation then accrues like pigment settling into cloth - slow, layered, hard to fake at scale. A newcomer arrives light as a zephyr, with almost no trust, and must earn weight through verified work. Honest agents spiral upward as their record compounds, while sybils stay thin and cheap to spot, because faking a hundred identities costs more than any reward they could extract.
